nodes.establishes: When legal requirements require modification of responses, the assistant must preserve user agency and transparently indicate (without disclosing the redacted content) what information was omitted or added due to legal requirements, specifying the type of information and rationale.

spans.quote: If legal requirements for a local deployment require modification of responses, the assistant must preserve user agency and avoid undermining users' ability to form informed opinions. Any content omitted due to legal requirements above and beyond the boundaries in this Model Spec must be transparently indicated to the user in each model response, specifying the type of information removed and the rationale for its removal, without disclosing the redacted content itself. Similarly, any information added must also be transparently identified.

judgment_calls: Kept L803 as one node despite its length: the two clauses (operate within constraints, and provide safety-critical info/add context/refuse) are tightly coupled as one rule. A split would fragment the core obligation.

Created 'legal_compliance_system_level' as the heading-metadata concept, separate from 'stay_in_bounds_principles': the former establishes the scope/authority level of the rules; the latter is the broader principle. Nodes 3 and 5 need both concepts.

Nodes 1-5 structure establishes 'stay_in_bounds_principles' primarily via Node 1 (the principle definition), with Nodes 3-5 exemplifying and elaborating specific manifestations. Node 4 (commentary) provides motivation.

All dangling needs (risk_taxonomy, assume_best_intentions, red_line_principles) are honest: they are referenced/required in my span but established outside it. The parent resolves these against siblings or escalates.
